title: Starter Initiative: Field Lab Playset
content:
Purpose
This is a lightweight, portable "playset" for running a first-touch SDK demo or field lab with nonengineer partners (CS, Solutions, Sales SEs). Goal: reliable 30–60 minute demo that surfaces core SDK value props (zero-config sample app, instrumented telemetry, predictable fallback behavior) and leaves a repeatable artifact the customer can run later.

Audience
- Solutions engineers and CS who need a low-friction demo for customers and POCs.
- Internal onboarding for new DevExp hires to learn a minimal integration loop.
- Small partner teams with limited infra (no K8s experience).

Success criteria (what counts as "ship")
- A single repo + three shell scripts that get a user from checkout -> authenticated -> sample-app running in under 10 minutes on macOS/Linux.
- Telemetry shows first successful request, latency, and token usage in Console within first five requests.
- Troubleshooting checklist reduces first-contact debug time to <15 minutes for SEs.
- At least one Solutions Engineer uses the playset in a customer call during the pilot week.

Constraints / Non-goals
- This is NOT a full SDK migration guide. It intentionally focuses on an extremely small happy path.
- No heavy production SSO or enterprise policy integrations in v1. Keep KMS/HSM and VPC options for follow-ups.

High-level pieces (packaged as the "playset")
1) starter-repo: minimal Node + Python sample app that demos text generate + embeddings + streaming. Includes sample prompts and a tiny UI.
2) get-started scripts: 3 scripts (install.sh, run-local.sh, demo-flow.sh) and a README quick flow.
3) telemetry hooks: example of event emission (first_request, fallback, error) + link to Console dashboard.
4) troubleshooting card: top 8 failure modes and commands to triage.
5) single-slide collateral: one-sheet with expected times, what to demo, and fallback talking points.

Flow (developer facing)
- install.sh (installs deps, sets env stub, checks node/python versions):
  - ./install.sh --quiet
- demo-flow.sh (guides user through: set API_KEY, run sample server, open local UI, run 3 pre-baked prompts)
  - ./demo-flow.sh --auto  # runs the three prompts and prints outputs
- run-local.sh (starts a tiny server-only UI for interactive prompts)
  - ./run-local.sh 3000

Key UX notes for SEs (talk track + checkpoints)
- First 2 minutes: confirm API key and region; show Console token/usage view.
- 3–5 minutes: run the 3 prompts to show generation latency and streaming. Mention cost/latency tradeoff (batching + quantized model variant) as a follow-up.
- 5–10 minutes: show embeddings sample (search or rerank) and where embeddings units show up in usage.
- If a customer asks about private deployments: do a quick diagram and schedule a dedicated follow-up.

Telemetry & observability (minimum viable)
- Emit custom events in the repo using the new lightweight client telemetry API: first_request, sample_prompt_sent, fallback_used, error_rate_event.
- Provide a pre-made Console query and dashboard link (see linked_artifacts) that filters by the demo repo tag.
- NOTE: telemetry calls must be idempotent in the demo; stash a demo_session_id in local .env to group events.

Troubleshooting cheat-card (top things to triage)
1) No network / API unreachable: curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health -> check 200
2) Invalid API key: run demo-flow.sh -> look for 401 in server logs, verify env var REDWOOD_API_KEY
3) Excessively slow first token: confirm model variant (gpt-*-realtime vs gpt-*-small), check regional mismatch; suggest small-quant model for demo.
4) Streaming not working: confirm SSE support in browser and demo server wired to response stream endpoint.
5) Embeddings mismatch: ensure embedding model name is same between client and query flow; sample code includes mapping constants.
6) Telemetry missing: ensure DEMO_SESSION_ID set, run events check in Console, fallback to local log file (demo-playset.log).
7) Local port collisions: run-local.sh checks and auto-increments.
8) Unexpected errors: collect server.log + network trace (curl -v) and file a ticket DEVEXP-314 with label "playset-debug".

Micro-iteration plan (week-by-week pilot)
- Week 0: prototype & script proof (internal devexp-only run). Owner: Asha.
- Week 1: field-test with 3 SEs, collect friction notes; add 2 telemetry events. Owner: Martin.
- Week 2: polish scripts, add slide one-sheet, create Confluence install guide. Owner: Priya.
- Week 3: public pilot with 10 customer demos; bug triage and 1st patch. Owner: Noah.

Open questions / TODOs
- Should the starter-repo include a prebuilt Docker image for folks on Windows? (low priority)
- Do we add a minimal OAuth flow in v1 to demo enterprise SSO? (likely v2)
- Decide on the demo default model variant and whether to surface a cost estimate inline.
- Add a short "what to record during demo" log template for CS to capture follow-ups.

Developer notes (implementation hints)
- Keep the sample app under 200 LOC per language (Node + Python). Use tiny frameworks (Fastify / Flask).
- Use fetch + EventSource on the client side for streaming example. Server should proxy to Redwood API and forward event stream.
- Provide a sample .env.template with placeholders and heuristics for region selection.
- Add a CI smoke test that attempts a demo-flow run using a test API_KEY (CI secrets vault) to prevent regressions in example flow.

Distribution & enablement
- Repo published under github.com/redwood-inference/playsets/starter-field-lab
- Create a short Loom (6–8 min) demonstrating full run-through for SE ramp.
- Add a template Intercom/CS note template so CS can attach the repo link post-call.

Appendix: Short demo script (for SEs)
- "Hello — thanks for the time. I’ll share my screen, we’ll run a tiny app that shows generation, streaming, and embeddings in 10 mins. I’ve already provisioned a demo key if you want to try later. If anything times out I’ll show how fallback routing keeps things working. After this, would you like the repo link and a short Loom?"

Quick links (for maintainers)
- Confluence field-lab index: https://confluence.redwood/team/devexp/field-lab-index
- Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/playsets/starter-field-lab (stubbed for now)
- Jira epic: https://jira.redwood/browse/DEVEXP-314

Notes to self (raw, keep this part informal)
- Keep friction surface tiny. Cut anything that adds >3 extra steps.
- If lots of customers ask about private deployment, spin a variant "playset-private-v1" that uses a local mock gateway.
- Record a quick video of the troubleshooting checklist in action — very helpful for new SEs.
- Follow up: capture pilot metrics (how many demos completed, average time to first sample output) and add to Confluence page.

-- end of doc --
